subtopics.name: Measuring length and volume
subtopics.detail: Using rulers, tapes and micrometers to measure lengths with appropriate precision. Using a measuring cylinder for liquid volume; displacement method for solids.

subtopics.name: Measuring time intervals
subtopics.detail: Measuring time intervals using clocks and digital timers; determining averages by measuring multiples.

subtopics.name: Scalars and vectors
subtopics.detail: Scalar: magnitude only (distance, speed, time, mass, energy, temperature). Vector: magnitude and direction (displacement, force, weight, velocity, acceleration, momentum, field strengths).

subtopics.name: Resultant of perpendicular vectors
subtopics.detail: Determining by calculation or graphically the resultant of two vectors at right angles (forces or velocities).

subtopics.name: Speed and velocity
subtopics.detail: Speed = distance / time. Velocity = change in displacement / time. Average speed = total distance / total time.

subtopics.name: Acceleration and deceleration
subtopics.detail: Acceleration = change in velocity / time. Deceleration is negative acceleration. Uniform and non-uniform acceleration.

subtopics.name: Distance-time graphs
subtopics.detail: Sketching, plotting and interpreting distance-time graphs. Gradient = speed. Identifying rest, constant speed, acceleration and deceleration.

subtopics.name: Speed-time graphs
subtopics.detail: Sketching, plotting and interpreting speed-time graphs. Gradient = acceleration; area = distance. Identifying constant and changing acceleration from graph shape.

subtopics.name: Acceleration of free fall
subtopics.detail: g ≈ 10 m/s² near Earth's surface. Uniform acceleration equations not required for O Level.

subtopics.name: Free fall and terminal velocity
subtopics.detail: Motion of objects falling with and without air/liquid resistance. Terminal velocity reached when drag equals weight.

subtopics.name: Mass and inertia
subtopics.detail: Mass measures quantity of matter and resists change in motion (inertia). Measured with an electronic balance or by comparison.

subtopics.name: Weight and gravitational field strength
subtopics.detail: Weight = gravitational force on an object with mass. g = W/m (gravitational field strength ≈ 10 N/kg near Earth). Equivalent to acceleration of free fall.

subtopics.name: Density definition and equation
subtopics.detail: Density = mass / volume (ρ = m/V). Units: kg/m³ or g/cm³.

subtopics.name: Measuring density experimentally
subtopics.detail: Determining density of a liquid, regularly shaped solid, and irregularly shaped solid (volume by displacement).

subtopics.name: Floating and sinking
subtopics.detail: Whether an object or liquid floats depends on density comparisons.

subtopics.name: Effects of forces and deformation
subtopics.detail: Forces may change size, shape or velocity of an object. Load-extension graphs for elastic solids (Hooke's Law region).

subtopics.name: Hooke's Law and spring constant
subtopics.detail: Spring constant k = F/x. Limit of proportionality: where Hooke's Law ceases to apply.

subtopics.name: Resultant forces
subtopics.detail: Resultant of coplanar forces; two forces along the same line; vector addition of perpendicular forces.

subtopics.name: Newton's Laws of motion
subtopics.detail: Newton's 1st Law: constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force. Newton's 2nd Law: F = ma. Newton's 3rd Law: equal and opposite forces on interacting objects.

subtopics.name: Friction and drag
subtopics.detail: Solid friction impedes motion and produces heating. Fluid friction (drag) acts on objects moving through liquids and gases.

subtopics.name: Moments and turning effects
subtopics.detail: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Everyday examples.

subtopics.name: Principle of moments
subtopics.detail: For equilibrium: sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments. Applied to one or more forces on each side of the pivot.

subtopics.name: Centre of gravity and stability
subtopics.detail: Centre of gravity: point where weight acts. Experimental determination for an irregular lamina. Stability and toppling.

topics.name: Momentum
keywords: resultant force acting for a time

subtopics.name: Momentum definition
subtopics.detail: Momentum p = mv. Unit: kg m/s.

subtopics.name: Conservation of momentum
subtopics.detail: Principle of conservation of momentum applied to simple one-dimensional collisions.

subtopics.name: Impulse and force
subtopics.detail: Resultant force = rate of change of momentum. Impulse = Ft = Δ(mv).

subtopics.name: Energy stores
subtopics.detail: Energy stored as kinetic, gravitational potential, chemical, elastic (strain), nuclear, electrostatic and internal (thermal).

subtopics.name: Energy transfers and conservation
subtopics.detail: Energy transferred by forces, electrical currents, heating and waves. Conservation of energy; flow diagrams.

subtopics.name: Kinetic and gravitational potential energy
subtopics.detail: Ek = ½mv². Ep = mgh. Energy conversions in free fall.

subtopics.name: Work done
subtopics.detail: Work done = force × distance in direction of force (W = Fd). Equals energy transferred.

subtopics.name: Energy resources
subtopics.detail: Fossil fuels, biofuels, hydroelectric, tidal, wave, geothermal, nuclear, solar (cells and panels), wind. Advantages and disadvantages: renewability, availability, reliability, scale, environmental impact.

subtopics.name: Power
subtopics.detail: Power = work done / time = energy transferred / time. P = W/t.

subtopics.name: Efficiency
subtopics.detail: Efficiency = useful energy output / total energy input (as a ratio or %). Represented in Sankey diagrams.

subtopics.name: Pressure definition and equation
subtopics.detail: Pressure = force / area (p = F/A). Everyday examples of how pressure varies with force and area.

subtopics.name: Pressure in liquids
subtopics.detail: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth: Δp = ρgh. Manometers and hydraulic systems.

subtopics.name: Atmospheric pressure
subtopics.detail: The atmosphere exerts pressure. Barometers measure atmospheric pressure.

subtopics.name: States of matter
subtopics.detail: Distinguishing properties of solids, liquids and gases. Terms for changes in state: melting, boiling, condensation, solidification.

subtopics.name: Particle model
subtopics.detail: Arrangement, separation and motion of particles in solids, liquids and gases. Simple particle diagrams.

subtopics.name: Brownian motion
subtopics.detail: Random motion of microscopic particles in suspension as evidence for the kinetic particle model.

subtopics.name: Gas pressure and temperature
subtopics.detail: Gas pressure from particle collisions. Qualitative effect of temperature change at constant volume; volume change at constant temperature.

subtopics.name: Absolute zero and the Kelvin scale
subtopics.detail: Absolute zero = −273 °C (particles have minimum kinetic energy). T (K) = θ (°C) + 273.

subtopics.name: Boyle's Law
subtopics.detail: pV = constant for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature. Graphical representation.

subtopics.name: Thermal expansion
subtopics.detail: Thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases. Everyday applications and consequences. Liquid-in-glass thermometer.

subtopics.name: Specific heat capacity
subtopics.detail: SHC = energy required per unit mass per unit temperature increase. E = mcθ. Experiments to measure SHC.

subtopics.name: Melting and boiling
subtopics.detail: Energy input at constant temperature during melting and boiling. Melting point and boiling point of water at standard pressure. Condensation and solidification described in terms of particles.

subtopics.name: Evaporation
subtopics.detail: More-energetic particles escape from a liquid surface, causing cooling. Factors: temperature, surface area, air movement.

subtopics.name: Latent heat
subtopics.detail: Specific latent heat of fusion and vaporisation: energy per unit mass for a change of state at constant temperature. l = E/m.

subtopics.name: Conduction
subtopics.detail: Experiments demonstrating good and bad thermal conductors. Conduction in solids: lattice vibrations and free electrons in metals.

subtopics.name: Convection
subtopics.detail: Convection in liquids and gases: density changes drive the current. Experiments to illustrate convection.

subtopics.name: Radiation (infrared)
subtopics.detail: All objects emit infrared radiation. Does not require a medium. Effect of surface colour and texture on emission, absorption and reflection.

subtopics.name: Good and bad emitters and absorbers
subtopics.detail: Experiments to distinguish good/bad emitters and absorbers. Rate of emission depends on surface temperature and area.

subtopics.name: Everyday applications
subtopics.detail: Applications: vacuum flask, solar panels, greenhouse effect, cooling fins, house insulation. Complex situations involving more than one mode.

subtopics.name: Energy transfer by waves
subtopics.detail: Waves transfer energy without transferring matter.

subtopics.name: Wave features
subtopics.detail: Wavefront, wavelength, frequency, crest, trough, amplitude and wave speed.

subtopics.name: Wave speed equation
subtopics.detail: v = fλ. Calculating wave speed, frequency or wavelength.

subtopics.name: Transverse and longitudinal waves
subtopics.detail: Transverse: vibration ⊥ propagation (EM waves, water, S-waves). Longitudinal: vibration ∥ propagation (sound, P-waves).

subtopics.name: Reflection, refraction and diffraction
subtopics.detail: Waves undergo reflection, refraction (change of speed) and diffraction. Ripple tank experiments.

subtopics.name: Diffraction effects
subtopics.detail: Effect of wavelength and gap size on diffraction through a gap; wavelength affects diffraction at an edge.

subtopics.name: Reflection and plane mirrors
subtopics.detail: Laws of reflection. Image in a plane mirror: same size, same distance, virtual. Simple constructions.

subtopics.name: Refraction of light
subtopics.detail: Refraction of light by transparent blocks. Passage of light at a boundary between two media.

subtopics.name: Total internal reflection
subtopics.detail: Critical angle; internal reflection and total internal reflection. Optical fibres in telecommunications.

subtopics.name: Thin lenses
subtopics.detail: Converging and diverging lenses. Focal length, principal axis, principal focus. Ray diagrams for real and virtual images. Image characteristics.

subtopics.name: Magnifying glass and vision correction
subtopics.detail: Single converging lens as a magnifying glass. Correcting long-sightedness and short-sightedness.

subtopics.name: Dispersion and colour
subtopics.detail: Dispersion of white light by a prism. Seven colours of the visible spectrum in order of frequency and wavelength.

subtopics.name: Refractive index
subtopics.detail: n = sin i / sin r. Relationship to critical angle: n = 1/sin c.

topics.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
keywords: speed of light in a vacuum

subtopics.name: Regions of the EM spectrum
subtopics.detail: Main regions in order of frequency (and wavelength): radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma. All travel at ~3.0 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.

subtopics.name: Uses of EM radiation
subtopics.detail: Radio, microwave, infrared, visible, UV, X-ray and gamma radiation — their typical uses and applications.

subtopics.name: Harmful effects of EM radiation
subtopics.detail: Microwaves: internal heating. Infrared: burns. UV: skin cancer, eye damage. X-rays and gamma: cell mutation/damage.

subtopics.name: Communication systems
subtopics.detail: Satellite communication by microwaves; mobile phones; Bluetooth (radio waves); optical fibres. Digital vs. analogue signals and benefits of digital.

subtopics.name: Production and nature of sound
subtopics.detail: Sound produced by vibrating sources. Longitudinal wave requiring a medium. Compressions and rarefactions.

subtopics.name: Speed of sound
subtopics.detail: Speed of sound in air ≈ 330–350 m/s. Method: measuring distance and time. Sound travels faster in denser media.

subtopics.name: Loudness, pitch and amplitude
subtopics.detail: Amplitude affects loudness; frequency affects pitch. Audible range: 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

subtopics.name: Echoes
subtopics.detail: Echo = reflection of sound waves. Calculation of depth/distance using speed and time.

subtopics.name: Ultrasound
subtopics.detail: Ultrasound: frequency > 20 kHz. Uses: non-destructive testing, medical scanning, sonar.

subtopics.name: Magnetic poles and forces
subtopics.detail: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract. Forces between magnets and magnetic materials. Induced magnetism.

subtopics.name: Magnetic and non-magnetic materials
subtopics.detail: Magnetic materials (iron, steel, nickel, cobalt). Distinguishing magnetic from non-magnetic.

subtopics.name: Temporary and permanent magnets
subtopics.detail: Soft iron: temporary magnets. Steel: permanent magnets. Magnetisation and demagnetisation methods.

subtopics.name: Magnetic fields and field lines
subtopics.detail: Magnetic field: region where a pole experiences a force. Drawing and plotting field lines around a bar magnet; field line spacing = relative strength.

subtopics.name: Uses of magnets
subtopics.detail: Applications of permanent magnets and electromagnets.

subtopics.name: Electric charge and static electricity
subtopics.detail: Positive and negative charges; like repel, unlike attract. Charging by friction (transfer of electrons). Detecting electrostatic charges.

subtopics.name: Conductors and insulators
subtopics.detail: Free electrons in conductors; bound electrons in insulators. Electron model to explain differences.

subtopics.name: Electric current
subtopics.detail: Current = charge / time. d.c. and a.c. Conventional current from + to −; electron flow from − to +. Using ammeters.

subtopics.name: Electromotive force and potential difference
subtopics.detail: e.m.f. = electrical work done per unit charge around a complete circuit. p.d. = work done per unit charge through a component. Both in volts.

subtopics.name: Resistance and Ohm's Law
subtopics.detail: R = V/I. Experiment to determine resistance. Current-voltage graphs for resistors, filament lamps and diodes.

subtopics.name: Resistance and dimensions
subtopics.detail: For a metallic conductor: resistance ∝ length; resistance ∝ 1/cross-sectional area.

subtopics.name: Electrical power and energy
subtopics.detail: P = IV; E = IVt. Kilowatt-hour. Cost of electrical energy. Circuits transfer energy from source to surroundings.

subtopics.name: Circuit symbols and components
subtopics.detail: Drawing and interpreting circuit diagrams: cells, batteries, switches, resistors, thermistors, LDRs, lamps, motors, ammeters, voltmeters, diodes, LEDs, transformers, fuses, relays.

subtopics.name: Series and parallel circuits
subtopics.detail: Series: same current throughout; p.d.s add; combined R = R₁ + R₂ + … Parallel: p.d. same across branches; currents add; combined R less than any branch.

subtopics.name: Kirchhoff's Laws
subtopics.detail: Sum of currents into a junction = sum out. Total p.d. in series = sum of individual p.d.s. Parallel p.d. equal across branches.

subtopics.name: Combining resistance
subtopics.detail: Calculated combined resistance for series and parallel arrangements.

subtopics.name: Potential divider
subtopics.detail: Action of a variable potential divider; equation for two resistors as a potential divider.

subtopics.name: Electrical hazards
subtopics.detail: Hazards of damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp conditions and overloading of plugs/extension leads.

subtopics.name: Mains wiring
subtopics.detail: Mains circuit: live, neutral and earth wires. Switch must be on the live side for safe disconnection.

subtopics.name: Fuses and circuit breakers
subtopics.detail: Operation of fuses and trip switches (circuit breakers); choosing appropriate ratings.

subtopics.name: Double insulation and earthing
subtopics.detail: Outer casing must be non-conducting (double-insulated) or earthed. Fuse without earth protects the cable for a double-insulated appliance.

subtopics.name: Electrical power and the kilowatt-hour
subtopics.detail: P = IV. kWh as unit of electrical energy. Calculating cost of electrical energy.

subtopics.name: Electromagnetic induction
subtopics.detail: A conductor moving through a magnetic field, or a changing field linking a conductor, induces an e.m.f. Lenz's Law: direction of induced e.m.f. opposes the change.

subtopics.name: Factors affecting induced e.m.f.
subtopics.detail: Magnitude affected by speed of movement, strength of field and number of turns.

subtopics.name: The AC generator
subtopics.detail: Simple a.c. generator (rotating coil or magnet); slip rings and brushes. e.m.f. vs. time graph.

subtopics.name: Magnetic field of a current
subtopics.detail: Pattern and direction of magnetic field around straight wires and solenoids. Experiments to map fields. Applications: relays and loudspeakers.

subtopics.name: Force on a current-carrying conductor
subtopics.detail: Experiment: force on a current in a magnetic field; effect of reversing current or field direction. Force on beams of charged particles.

subtopics.name: The DC motor
subtopics.detail: Current-carrying coil in a field experiences a turning effect. DC motor: split-ring commutator and brushes.

subtopics.name: Transformers
subtopics.detail: Construction: soft-iron core, primary and secondary coils. Step-up and step-down. Turns ratio: Vₚ/Vₛ = Nₚ/Nₛ. Transformer efficiency: VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ.

subtopics.name: High-voltage electricity transmission
subtopics.detail: Transformers in high-voltage transmission. High voltage reduces current and therefore power losses (P = I²R).

subtopics.name: Displaying waveforms
subtopics.detail: Using an oscilloscope to display the waveform of a signal. Reading amplitude and time period from the screen.

subtopics.name: Measuring voltage and frequency
subtopics.detail: Calculating peak voltage and frequency from oscilloscope traces. Comparing d.c. and a.c. waveforms.

subtopics.name: Atomic structure
subtopics.detail: Atom: positively charged nucleus surrounded by orbiting electrons. Nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

subtopics.name: Protons, neutrons and electrons
subtopics.detail: Relative charges: proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1. Atoms form ions by gaining or losing electrons.

subtopics.name: Proton number and nucleon number
subtopics.detail: Proton (atomic) number Z; nucleon (mass) number A. Number of neutrons = A − Z. Nuclide notation ᴬZ X.

subtopics.name: Isotopes
subtopics.detail: Isotopes: same element, same proton number, different nucleon numbers.

subtopics.name: Alpha particle scattering
subtopics.detail: α particle scattering by thin metal: evidence for a small, dense, positive nucleus surrounded by mostly empty space.

subtopics.name: Nuclear fission and fusion
subtopics.detail: Fission: heavy nucleus splits, releasing energy. Fusion: light nuclei join, releasing energy. Nuclide equations; qualitative mass-energy changes.

subtopics.name: Background radiation
subtopics.detail: Sources: radon gas, rocks/buildings, food/drink, cosmic rays. Correcting count rates for background.

subtopics.name: Types of nuclear emission
subtopics.detail: Alpha (α), beta (β) and gamma (γ) radiation. Emission is spontaneous and random.

subtopics.name: Properties of radiation
subtopics.detail: Penetrating power and range in air. Deflection in electric and magnetic fields. Relative ionising effects.

subtopics.name: Radioactive decay
subtopics.detail: Spontaneous, random change in an unstable nucleus. α or β emission changes the element. Decay equations using nuclide notation.

subtopics.name: Half-life
subtopics.detail: Half-life: time for half the nuclei of an isotope to decay. Simple calculations using tables or decay curves.

subtopics.name: Uses of radioactive isotopes
subtopics.detail: Smoke alarms, food irradiation, equipment sterilisation, thickness gauging, cancer diagnosis and treatment. Choice depends on radiation type and half-life.

subtopics.name: Radiation safety
subtopics.detail: Effects: cell death, mutation, cancer. Safe handling, storage and transport. Precautions: reduce time, increase distance, use shielding.

subtopics.name: Earth's rotation and day/night
subtopics.detail: Earth rotates on its tilted axis once every ~24 hours, explaining apparent daily motion of the Sun and day/night cycle.

subtopics.name: Earth's orbit and the seasons
subtopics.detail: Earth orbits the Sun in ~365 days; axial tilt explains seasons.

subtopics.name: The Moon's orbit and phases
subtopics.detail: The Moon orbits Earth in ~one month, explaining the cycle of lunar phases.

subtopics.name: The Solar System
subtopics.detail: Sun, eight planets (and order), dwarf planets, asteroids, moons, comets. Orbits are elliptical.

subtopics.name: Gravitational fields in the Solar System
subtopics.detail: Sun's gravity keeps planets in orbit. Gravitational field strength depends on mass and decreases with distance. Orbital speeds decrease with distance from the Sun.

subtopics.name: Orbital speed and light travel time
subtopics.detail: Average orbital speed: v = 2πr/T. Calculating time for light to travel between Solar System objects.

subtopics.name: The Sun as a star
subtopics.detail: The Sun is a medium-sized star, mostly hydrogen and helium. Stars are powered by nuclear fusion (H → He).

subtopics.name: Life cycle of a star
subtopics.detail: Interstellar cloud → protostar → stable star → red giant/supergiant → white dwarf (less massive) or supernova/neutron star/black hole (more massive).

subtopics.name: Scale of the Universe
subtopics.detail: One light-year = 9.5 × 10¹⁵ m. The Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies; diameter ≈ 100 000 light-years.

subtopics.name: Redshift and the expanding Universe
subtopics.detail: Redshift: observed wavelength increases from receding galaxies. Evidence that the Universe is expanding; supports the Big Bang Theory.

subtopics.name: Cosmic microwave background radiation
subtopics.detail: CMBR: microwave radiation from all directions, produced shortly after the Big Bang, stretched into the microwave region as the Universe expanded.

subtopics.name: The Hubble constant and age of the Universe
subtopics.detail: H = v/d. 1/H estimates the age of the Universe — evidence all matter was once at a single point.
